concept.name: Random forest
concept.definition: A bagged ensemble of decision trees that also randomizes the candidate features considered at splits, reducing correlation among trees.
concept.intuition: It is a learnable mapping or representation used to turn features into predictions or groups.
concept.mechanics: Bootstrap rows for each tree, choose splits from random feature subsets, grow many trees, then average regression values or vote on classes.
concept.failure_modes: Flexible models can fit noise, shift under new regimes, and conceal instability when tuning is repeated on the same validation data.
concept.misconceptions: Greater model complexity or in-sample accuracy does not by itself imply better out-of-sample trading results.
concept.example: Five hundred trees each consider sqrt(p) features per split; 310 vote for an up day, producing class 1.
